figure_discussions.title: Illustrative level response to a feed-rate step
figure_discussions.observation: Separator Level: liquid level spans 50–54.98 % across the plotted cases. Valve Position: valve opening spans 50–67.48 % across the plotted cases.
figure_discussions.mechanism: In the illustrative Python inventory balance, a higher level commands a larger outlet opening, removing the excess inventory after the feed step.
figure_discussions.implication: The trajectory explains controller action; it is not a NeqSim transient vessel validation.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Use a validated vessel inventory and energy model before transferring controller gains to plant equipment.
figure_discussions.editorial_review: Plot-specific interpretation reviewed against executed source and numerical data.

figure_discussions.caption: Illustrative level control: proportional-gain comparison. Illustrative Python inventory and control model.
figure_discussions.title: Illustrative level control: proportional-gain comparison
figure_discussions.observation: Kp = 50.0: liquid level spans 50–64.48 % across the plotted cases. Kp = 200.0: liquid level spans 50–54.98 % across the plotted cases.
figure_discussions.mechanism: Increasing the proportional gain makes the illustrative controller respond more strongly to a level error.
figure_discussions.implication: The smaller excursion here is conditional on the simplified process response and absence of realistic actuator limits and noise.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Repeat the tuning study with valve travel, measurement delay and plant dynamics before deployment.
